sections.h2: Can a Dunedin house sell quickly for cash?
sections.html:
Yes. A cash buyer skips the loan approval and the appraisal, so a Dunedin sale can close as fast as the title search and any payoff letters allow. What slows most sales is the house itself: repairs, a tenant, an estate or a lender deadline.

Dunedin sits on the Gulf side of Pinellas County, north of Clearwater and St. Petersburg. The city's own description calls it one of the few open waterfront communities between Sarasota and Cedar Key where buildings leave the water visible. Selling directly means no inspection-driven repair list to argue over.

The sections below cover the town itself, the Pinellas homestead rules that change after a sale, the deed costs set by the state and the steps to get a deed recorded.

sections.h2: Who buys homes in Dunedin and why?
sections.html:
Dunedin pulls interest from people who like a walkable town. The city's history page says the area was first called Jonesboro after the owner of a general store, then renamed in 1882 when two Scottish merchants petitioned for a post office called Dunedin, from the Gaelic for castle on the rock. It became an incorporated town on June 1, 1899 and a city in 1925.

The city reports more than 35,000 residents as of 2025, and Scottish touches run through street and neighborhood names such as Scotland Street, Louden Avenue and Brae-Moor. It bills itself as the Best Little Walking Town in America.

  • Honeymoon Island State Park is a short drive from downtown.
  • TD Ballpark hosts the Toronto Blue Jays for Spring Training.
  • Dunedin was the first Florida city named a Trail Town.
  • The city says it was the first Florida city to reach platinum status in a green-building program for local governments.

Those draws attract three kinds of buyers: people who want to live near downtown, second-home owners who want the beaches, and investors. A cash buyer can serve any of them without asking you to stage the house.

sections.h2: What does the Pinellas Property Appraiser say about homestead?
sections.html:
The Pinellas County Property Appraiser prints the homestead benefit as $51,411 off assessed value. The first $25,000 reaches every tax on the bill, and the remaining $26,411 applies to value between $50,000 and $75,000 and leaves out school taxes.

Your exemption ends when you sell. The appraiser lists a sale, renting the property, any change of ownership and no longer living there as the events that stop it. A buyer who closes after January 1 may still see your homestead on the August notice, and that credit disappears on December 31. The buyer then files an original application, due by March 1, to start their own.

The assessment cap also restarts for the buyer, so the state returns the property to just value on the next January 1. If you are buying elsewhere in Florida, ask about portability, which carries part of your capped benefit to a new homestead established within three years.

sections.h2: What fixed costs come with a Dunedin sale?
sections.html:
State and county charges are set by law, so you can see them before you list. The biggest is usually the deed stamp tax, which the state prints at 70 cents on each $100 of consideration everywhere except Miami-Dade. Every party to the deed is liable, though the contract normally assigns it to the seller.

The Pinellas clerk also charges a per-page fee for recording under section 28.24: $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, with separate technology and trust fund add-ons. Confirm the total with the clerk.

sections.h2: What does a new Pinellas owner bring to file for homestead?
sections.html:
The appraiser's office asks for proof of residency for every owner, spouses included. Its list covers a Florida driver license and auto registration, a voter card or permanent resident card if one applies, and Social Security numbers for all owners and spouses, even if only one spouse is on the deed.

If you hold another residency-based exemption in Florida or another state, the application will be denied. The office asks for proof that the other exemption was removed, or a copy of the latest tax bill for any property owned elsewhere, within 30 days of applying.

  • You can file online or in person at one of the appraiser's offices.
  • If you received homestead last year and still live there, a receipt arrives in early January.
  • Tell the office if you stop qualifying, for example after renting the home out.

Pass this list to your buyer. A quick, correct filing keeps their first tax bill predictable.

sections.h2: How is a Dunedin deed signed and recorded?
sections.html:
Florida law requires a deed to be in writing and witnessed by two people, and section 689.01 permits witnessing over audio-video technology. Closing agents normally draft the deed and carry it to the clerk.

  1. Sign the sales contract and open a title order.
  2. Clear liens, loan payoffs and any open permits the search turns up.
  3. Sign the deed before two witnesses.
  4. Pay stamps and recording fees to the clerk.
  5. Let the appraiser update the tax roll afterward.

Estate sales follow a different path. The Department of Revenue lists a personal representative's deed under a probated will as not taxable, while quitclaims and deeds given to a lender in place of foreclosure do carry stamp tax.

sections.h2: What if taxes or the mortgage are behind in Dunedin?
sections.html:
Act before the legal clock runs. Florida tax bills arrive in November, and the state's early-payment discount steps down from 4 percent that month to 1 percent in February. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1, and the tax collector sells certificates on them by June 1.

Foreclosure moves through the courts. After a final judgment the clerk holds a public sale between 20 and 35 days later unless the plaintiff agrees to wait longer, and the winning bidder puts down 5 percent. Selling first can retire the loan and leave any equity with you. If a sale has already happened, the clerk explains how surplus funds are claimed.

  • Ask the Pinellas Tax Collector about installment and deferral options.
  • Request a written payoff from your lender.
  • Speak with the clerk about surplus after a sale.

sections.h2: Should I sell for cash or list the house?
sections.html:
Compare what you keep, not just the offer. A listing may reach a higher price, yet it adds showings, repair negotiations, financing risk and months of carrying costs. A cash purchase moves fast, and the buyer accepts the property in its present state.

Use the closing statement from the title company to check each side: loan payoff, stamps, recording, unpaid taxes and the repairs you would otherwise fund. For recent nearby sales, search the Pinellas Property Appraiser's public records or ask a local agent.

faqs.q: Who pays deed stamps on a Dunedin sale?
faqs.a: The contract usually puts it on the seller, though the state makes every party to the deed liable. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected by the clerk.

faqs.q: Will the buyer inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. It ends with the sale. The new owner applies to the Pinellas Property Appraiser by March 1, and a leftover homestead on a notice is removed on December 31.

faqs.q: Can I sell with a tenant living in the house?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease still binds the parties, and a month-to-month tenancy needs at least 30 days' notice to end. Read the lease first.

faqs.q: What happens to my Save Our Homes savings?
faqs.a: The buyer does not get them. The property goes back to just value on the next January 1. You may move your own benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability.
The Pinellas clerk's recording office. The closing agent usually files it.
